Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old woman with new-onset left-sided posterior headache since yesterday, throbbing and severe (8/10), without red flag features; advised trial of stronger analgesia (in lieu of ibuprofen) plus acetaminophen, rest/hydration, and safety-net follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache.
- Onset/duration: Began yesterday mid-morning; gradual build-up over a short period.
- Location/character: Left posterior head; throbbing; intense.
- Severity: 8/10.
- Course: Persistent since onset; not worse at any particular time of day; able to sleep through the night.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: No change with lying down, standing, bending over, coughing, or sneezing. Ibuprofen (Nurofen) taken yesterday with no relief.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Denies nausea, vomiting.
  - Denies tingling, numbness, weakness.
  - Denies blurred vision, eye pain, visual phenomena (“funny lights”), photophobia.
  - Denies fever, chills/sweats, rash.
  - Eating and drinking as normal.
- Prior history of headaches: None; unusual for her to have headaches.
- Impact on function: Finding it hard to do work and normal activities.
- Blood pressure: Not checked recently.
- Triggers/lifestyle changes: Denies increased stress, or diet/lifestyle changes.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical problems reported.
- Denies asthma or stomach problems.

Medications:
- Current/Recent:
  - Ibuprofen (Nurofen) taken yesterday; dose/route/frequency not documented; no relief.
  - New prescription: “Stronger pain relief similar to ibuprofen” to be taken instead of ibuprofen and regularly with food; name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - May take acetaminophen (paracetamol) concurrently; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Designer.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Does not drink alcohol.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
- Mother: Hypertension; migraines.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented (telemedicine visit; no in-person exam reported).

Investigations:
- None reported or ordered during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute left-sided headache, new onset, throbbing, severe; no red flag features elicited; no prior headache history; nonresponsive to single dose of ibuprofen.
  - Plan:
    - Start prescribed stronger analgesic (NSAID-like) instead of ibuprofen; take regularly with food (specific medication and dosing not documented).
    - May use acetaminophen concomitantly for additional pain control.
    - Rest and maintain good hydration.
    - Safety-netting: Seek care if pain worsens, new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness), or if recurrent episodes occur.
    - Follow-up: If not improving or not settling within 1–2 days after trying prescribed medication, contact clinic for reassessment and next steps.

General Plan items:
- Return precautions and review within 1–2 days if no improvement.
- Consider in-person evaluation (including vitals and neurologic exam, and blood pressure measurement) if symptoms persist or worsen.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergy status not explicitly confirmed; medication name/dose/route/frequency for new prescription not documented; no vitals; no focused neurologic exam; no blood pressure measurement; pregnancy status not assessed.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses/fillers but clinically adequate.
